steps.text: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).

Whisk flour, 2 teaspoons sugar, and 1 teaspoon salt together in a 9-inch pie plate; make a well in the center. Pour ½ cup oil and 2 tablespoons rice milk into well; mix with a fork until a dough forms. Press evenly into the bottom and up sides of the pie plate using your hands; crimp edges of crust.

Combine ½ cup white sugar, brown sugar, cinnamon, ½ teaspoon salt, ginger, nutmeg, and cloves in a large bowl; set aside. Whisk pumpkin purée, 1 ¼ cups rice milk, eggs, 2 tablespoons oil, and vanilla together in a separate bowl until combined; stir into sugar mixture until fully combined. Pour filling into the prepared crust; place on a baking sheet.

Bake in the preheated oven for 10 minutes. Reduce the oven temperature to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C); continue baking until a knife inserted near the center comes out clean, 40 to 50 minutes more. The center may still wiggle a little but will firm up once out of the oven. Cool on a wire rack.

raw_recipe.headline: Killer Pumpkin Pie
raw_recipe.description: This "Killer Pumpkin Pie" recipe is dairy—and soy-free. It uses rice milk, pumpkin purée, brown and white sugar, cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, and cloves.
raw_recipe.name: Killer Pumpkin Pie

review.reviewBody: It's the crust I want to rate/review. I've been using this crust recipe for years as I'm not very good at making rolled crusts. This is soooo easy and is very flaky. If using it in an 8" inch pan, reserve some of the dough to crumble on the top of the filling--almost a double crust pie! The double baking time helps keep the bottom from getting soggy, even with juicy fruit pies!

I didn’t make the crust because I’m doing a very low carb diet. 
Finally a wonderful pumpkin pie I can make w/unsweetened almond milk! I used Trivia brown sugar & Trivia white sugar in place of sugar (because I’m diabetic) I used two whole eggs and one egg yolk to thicken up the 1 cup of unsweetened almond milk that I used. I used a 1/4 cup of Half and half as well. (I can have dairy, but not the sugar in it) 
I cooked the pie on high in a glass pan for four minutes (no crust) in the microwave . then I cooked it in the oven (after whisking) at 400 for 15 minutes and then 350° for an hour. 
It turned out perfect! My new go to pie!

Only made the filling and added it to a GF graham cracker crust. Used cashew milk instead and consistency was lovely. Next time I will omit the ginger and cloves as it ended up tasting more gingerbread-like; the pumpkin didn't shine through as well as I had hoped. Baked in a convection oven at 400 degrees for 10 min, then reduced to 325 for an additional 30-35 minutes. Other reviewers said they needed to back for longer than directed, but I found the pie was set and the middle quivery using the above time frame.

This recipe was awesome! Thank you 'BakesCakes' for the inspiration. We are trying to omit as much dairy as possible and I needed to use up some pumpkin that I froze last Fall. I made my own crust, but I am excited to try this version. Working with pre-frozen pumpkin, I thought I'd need to make up for the extra water so I decreased the milk to only 1 cup. For the rest of the filling, based on comments that it came out a little less "set" than the traditional recipe, I omitted the oil. I also halved the cinnamon per reviewer comments. And the kicker...I added a heaping tablespoon of cashew cream (raw, soaked, rinsed, the purreed with water) hoping it would give the recipe the 'fat' that was missing from the diary. It baked at 425 for 20 mins, then 350 for 1 hour. The result? A perfectly set, firm pumpkin pie. It is absolutely unnoticeable that it is any different from traditional pumpkin pie. Thanks again 'BakesCakes.'

This was so much better than the traditional dairy-laden condensed milk version! Great pumpkin flavor. And I normally don’t really enjoy pumpkin pie. My substitutes: pumpkin pie spice for the ala carte spices, cashew milk for rice milk, and frozen prepared crust (I needed to whittle down time/effort, but am eager to try this crust sometime). There was too much filling for the crust, so I baked two ramekins of filling along with the pie. I gave this recipe only 4 stars because the baking time is off— it needed much more time to firm up. Just keep an eye on your crust and cover edges with foil if they finish before the pie does. But the recipe is a dairy-free winner!

I baked this pie for a get-together with my boyfriend's friends. My boyfriend can't eat gluten, corn, or milk, so pumpkin pie has been difficult for him. We only made a few adjustments, according to his dietary restrictions and other reviews on this recipe. We substituted cashew milk for rice milk (his preference) and decreased the amount of oil in the filling. We also substituted Red Mill gluten-free all-purpose flour for the crust, but made no other changes to the crust. As others have mentioned, we had to cook it a bit longer than the recipe suggests. This pie was so amazing! Everyone absolutely loved it! The pumpkin pie filling was just right, and I heard so many comments about the crust. This will be my go-to pumpkin pie from now on. Thank you so much for sharing this recipe!!!

I read a lot of reviews and made changes as necessary:
1) Used 3/4 cup full fat coconut milk (my can also had guar gum in it which probably helped to thicken it as well) And 1/2 cup rice milk.
2) used 1tbsp pumpkin pie spice instead of individual spices
3) baked at 425 for 20 minutes and 40-50 at 350 (I’m located in NY)
4) I omitted the oil
5) I used a premade gluten free shell

Fantastic recipe!! Thank you!!! I made it straight from the directions the first time (used a store bought crust though because I was super short on time). The center didn't get quite done enough before my crust started to blacken slightly... so the second time I followed user tips and baked for 15min on 425 before lowering to 350 for an hour. I also omitted the oil on the second pie and substituted the extra 1/3 rice milk for 1/3 sweetened condensed coconut milk and wow-so delish!!

Used 1/4 cup coconut cream and 1 cup coconut milk (light) for the rice milk. Left out the oil. Used 2 tsp. of pumpkin pie spice instead of the ginger, cinnamon, nutmeg and clove. Baked for 20 minutes at 425 then 40 minutes at 350. Kept checking every ten minutes until utensil came out clean. Used a homemade gingersnap/graham cracker crust using coconut cream instead of butter to bind. One of the best pumpkin pies that I have ever had! Thank you!

I made this recipe. It was absolutely delicious. However, I used a ready made Gluten Free crust from "Longos". I also substituted the pumpkin for a butternut squash. I cut and roasted the squash, let it cool, then scooped out 2 cups and used that in the recipe.
Everyone loved the pie. I will definitely make it again!

I made this tonight using oat milk instead of rice milk - and used about two cups of roasted pumpkin instead of canned. took about 30-45 minutes longer to set in the oven (at least 90+ minutes total of cooking time). Was truly the best dairy-free pie I have ever made - my family didn't even realize there was no dairy - even got compliments on the crust! Will definitely make again - however I may have to either cook some liquid off the pumpkin or use less "milk" in the future.

Just love this pumpkin pie recipe! I’ve brought it for desert after dinner at friends home and everyone loves it! I don’t mention I’m allergic to dairy and gluten. I just enjoy having dessert with everyone! I dont do the pie crust. I use Wholly Gluten Free frozen pie crust GF DF.

I have been baking pumpkin pies for 24 years, and this is now my favorite recipe yet. The spices are perfect. We have a severe dairy allergy, and I love using canned coconut milk as a milk substitute when baking. In this recipe, it's a sublime result. It adds thickness to the texture and the subtle coconut just contributes to a rich flavor.
First time making pie this is going to be delicious!

I make this every year for my grand who is dairy sensitive 
Thank you for this recipe .. it is so good
scrumptious. Did 1.5 teaspoons of cinnamon instead of 2
I liked how the spices and pumpkin flavors were equally balanced.
Used a store bought gluten free pie crust and used almond milk instead of rice milk and it turned out great! Took a little longer to cook but that’s ok! Definitely will make again.
This was really good pumpkin pie. I whipped it up while we ate our meal . Was pretty delish.

Amazing! I've always done the premade pies or crusts before and just picked around the thick cardboard tasting crusts. Never again! The flaky crust this recipe makes was my favorite part even though the pumpkin filling was also wonderful. I used unsweetened soymilk and made the crust using whole wheat flour. I used oil in the crust, but substituted cinnamon applesauce for the oil in the filling. Turned out absolutely delicious. Thank you for this great vegan-friendly recipe!
